bio.en: Anton Osika is co-founder and CEO of Lovable, an AI engineer that turns an English prompt into a working product in minutes, and the fastest-growing startup in Europe's history.
bio.zh: Anton Osika 是 Lovable 的联合创始人兼 CEO，Lovable 是一个把英文提示词在几分钟内变成可用产品的 AI“软件工程师”，也是欧洲史上增长最快的创业公司。

summary.en: Anton explains Lovable's origin and his philosophy of the “minimum lovable product,” arguing that being loved by users—not just used—is the real growth driver. He hit $10M ARR in two months with just 15 people by obsessing over generalist, multi-skilled hires rather than narrow roles. The conversation covers a live demo, how the team operates and hires, and which skills will matter more or less as AI product-building goes mainstream.

Then some engineer when was on call, maybe they woke up in the night and they saw their servers were taking too much load because of us. So then they shut off down completely and we got this email that said, "Oh, you broke some kind of rules and we didn't know what was going on."
turns.zh: 正确的。是的。所以这是后来的事情。那是和可爱的。所以这是可爱的。 Lovable，早些时候总是在有人使用 Lovable 时在 GitHub 上创建新项目，我们问他们，“可以吗？这里的限制如何？”他们说：“哦，没有限制。”但一旦我们开始每天创建 15,000 个项目，就会出现大量使用。然后一些工程师在值班时，也许他们在半夜醒来，发现他们的服务器因为我们而承受了太多的负载。然后他们完全关闭了，我们收到这封电子邮件，上面写着：“哦，你违反了某种规则，我们不知道发生了什么。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's similar to a story I heard when ChatGPT was originally being trained, Microsoft servers blocked it because they thought it was some crawler and it was just actually the very first version ChatGPT being trained on data. Anyway, keep going.
turns.zh: 这类似于我在 ChatGPT 最初接受训练时听到的一个故事，微软服务器阻止了它，因为他们认为这是某种爬虫，而这实际上只是在数据上训练的第一个版本的 ChatGPT。不管怎样，继续吧。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: So I built this tool called GPT Engineer and I was thinking about we're seeing the biggest change humanity will ever see, I think, where before you had the manual labor being taken over by machines, but now it's actually cognitive labor being done better than humans by machines and what's the best way to have some kind of positive impact here? It's not to make engineers more productive, which there's a lot of companies using AI to make engineers more productive, Microsoft did with co-pilot and so on. But it is to enable those who have such a hard time finding people who are good at creating software that's been their absolute bottleneck and let them take their ideas and their beliefs into reality. So enabling more entrepreneurship and innovation by building the AI software engineer for anyone. And then I grabbed a previous colleague of mine who has also been a founder, Fabian, and I said we should build something like GPT Engineer but it has to be for the people who don't write code and that's the story.
turns.zh: 因此，我构建了这个名为 GPT Engineer 的工具，我在想，我们正在看到人类将看到的最大变化，我认为，之前的体力劳动被机器接管，但现在实际上是机器比人类做得更好的认知劳动，在这里产生某种积极影响的最佳方式是什么？这并不是为了提高工程师的工作效率，很多公司都在使用人工智能来提高工程师的工作效率，微软就用副驾驶等方式做到了这一点。但它是为了帮助那些很难找到擅长创建软件的人（这一直是他们的绝对瓶颈）的人，让他们将自己的想法和信念变成现实。因此，通过为任何人培养人工智能软件工程师来促进更多的创业和创新。然后我找到了我以前的同事 Fabian，他也是创始人，我说我们应该构建类似 GPT Engineer 的东西，但它必须是为那些不编写代码的人设计的，这就是故事。

turns.en: Okay. And then that became lovable? There's the shift from open source into a product that anyone can use but also pay for. Makes sense. Okay, so from that point I saw a stat that you started making a million dollars in ARR per week and once you launched lovable, is that true?
turns.zh: 好的。然后就变得可爱了？从开源到任何人都可以使用但需要付费的产品的转变。有道理。好吧，从那时起我看到一个统计数据，你开始每周赚取 100 万美元的 ARR，一旦你推出了 lovely，这是真的吗？

We just hit 1 million ARR in a week and then it kept growing at that pace. It still growing at even faster than that pace.
turns.zh: 是的，如此推出，我们实际上将产品的第一个版本称为 GPT 工程师应用程序，它在某些方面非常不同，我们在候补名单下推出了它，并说，哦，是的，我们有这个候补名单，我们得到了很多反馈并进行了迭代。最后，当我们认为这个产品真的很好时，我们说好吧，现在我们有了一个可爱的产品。我们主要是在人工智能方面做了很多改进，一旦我们推出它，那是11月21日，所以那是差不多三个月前的事了。我们在一周内达到了 100 万 ARR，然后它继续以这个速度增长。它的增长速度甚至比这个速度还要快。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Faster than 1 million ARR per week. Holy shit.
turns.zh: 每周 ARR 快于 100 万。天哪。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Okay, that sounds like product market fit to me. You said that you did a lot of work on the backend. turns.zh: 好吧，这听起来像是适合我的产品市场。你说你在后端做了很多工作。我看到你发推文说你们想出了某种可扩展性的解锁方法，比如一个新的扩展法则，允许你构建这样的东西。您能在技术元素上谈论哪些内容让您能够构建出新的、成功的东西？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: There are many scaling laws I would say when you build AI systems and this one in particular is about when you put in more work, the product reliably gets better and better. And what you've seen generally when you have AI building something is that it can get stuck in some place. It is super good in the beginning and then it gets stuck. What we did was to painstakingly identify places where it got stuck and there is different approaches but address different ways how we do it but address the places where it gets stuck, tune the entire system quantitatively and having a very fast feedback loop to improve it in the areas where it got stuck. The most important areas, it still does get stuck sometimes, but that's the scaling law and we're still early in that scaling law, I would say.
turns.zh: 当你构建人工智能系统时，我会说有很多缩放法则，尤其是当你投入更多工作时，产品会变得越来越好。当你让人工智能构建一些东西时，你通常会看到它可能会卡在某个地方。一开始非常好，然后就卡住了。我们所做的就是煞费苦心地找出卡住的地方，有不同的方法，但解决我们如何做的不同方式，但要解决卡住的地方，定量地调整整个系统，并有一个非常快的反馈循环来改进卡住的地方。最重要的领域，有时它仍然会陷入困境，但这就是缩放定律，我想说，我们仍处于缩放定律的早期阶段。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so when you talk about things getting stuck, it's like the AI agent just saying, I don't know what to do from this point or they introduce some kind of bug. Is that an example of getting stuck?
turns.zh: 因此，当你谈论事情陷入困境时，就像人工智能代理只是说，我不知道从现在开始该做什么，或者他们引入了某种错误。这是一个陷入困境的例子吗？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: Yeah. It introduces some kind of bug and then it's not smart enough to figure out how to get out of that bug.
turns.zh: 是的。它引入了某种错误，然后它不够聪明，无法弄清楚如何摆脱该错误。

turns.en: I see. And this is a common problem people have with tools like this is they get to a certain point and then it's like, "Well I don't know what to do. turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: This is something that is a problem today and the frontier of where this is a problem is very rapidly receding back. This experience just going to not get stuck.
turns.zh: 这是当今的一个问题，而且这个问题的边界正在迅速后退。所以我们所做的就是确定最重要的领域，特别是添加登录、创建数据持久性、添加 Stripe 付款。例如，我们要确保它不会被卡住。今天卡住的地方目前是你可以很好地理解和摆脱卡住的地方，但在未来它不会那么重要。这种体验不会被卡住。

turns.en: I mean the team is everything in building a great product, so I just give a big shout-out to the team that has written the code. I haven't written much of the code recently, I would say. turns.en: The packaging for non-technical people is what we aim for and I showed you in the demo that you can edit the text, you can change the colors and so on instantly without having to go into the code editor and without having to wait about 30 seconds for the AI do the full change. (00:35:48): Not getting stuck is I think the most important thing for people. turns.zh: 面向非技术人员的包装是我们的目标，我在演示中向您展示了您可以立即编辑文本、更改颜色等，而无需进入代码编辑器，也无需等待大约 30 秒让 AI 完成完整的更改。这就是我们考虑包装它的重要方式。然后确保它可以在更大的团队中尽可能高效地使用。与我认为所有其他工具不同的是，它与 GitHub 同步，这意味着您可以使用 Cursor，或者团队中想要更底层的人可以使用 Cursor，而不想搞乱并设置本地文件系统并提交到 GitHub 等的人可以使用 Lovable。 (00:35:48)：我认为对人们来说最重要的是不陷入困境。这就是为什么我们进入这个领域较晚，我们没有像其他许多人那样进行相同类型的营销，但从我交谈过的人看来，我们仍然被评为最可靠的营销方式。

turns.en: Yeah.

(00:49:32): They might be entangled in technical details of like, "Okay, yes, this is the biggest problem, but we should have this larger technical initiative that's going to solve all of these problems." turns.zh: 只是顶线吗？我认为确定最大的瓶颈是什么，最大的问题是什么，然后快速迭代说：“好吧，这是最大的问题，让我们真正真正地解决这个问题。”然后选择下一个，不要过度思考，不要梦想出漫长的路线图，这就是我的[听不清 00:48:41]。有一个非常非常简单的算法。我认为理解什么是最大的问题并不总是一个简单的问题。是的，所以我们花时间与用户交谈，阅读人们所写的内容。正如您所说，我们有一个功能板，可以让人们提出很多请求。然后，当我们选择其中一个问题时，我们是相当以工程为主导的。对于我们这样的产品，很难让不是工程师的产品经理说，哦，这就是我们现在应该做的，因为问题的正确解决方案可能会纠缠在技术细节的东西上。 (00:49:32)：他们可能会纠结于技术细节，比如“好吧，是的，这是最大的问题，但我们应该有一个更大的技术举措来解决所有这些问题。”因此，与许多其他产品公司相比，它相当以工程为主导。

These are the things we're focusing on. This week, it's mostly... There's a good word for this that I would want your help with, but polish, we were fixing the bugs and polish this week and that was the planning on Monday.
turns.zh: 如果你回顾三个月，我们主要是说，“好吧，让我们做这个每周计划。”我们确实有一个大的堵塞板，其中包含所有主要问题，然后我们对它们进行了排序，我们还关注哪些，或者下周或本周我们关注什么？然后我们有一个演示，我们说：“好吧，这些是我们本周发布的东西。”因此，为了让每个人都达成共识，我们现在确实有更多的路线图，我们说我们将确保您可以支持自定义域。接下来，他们将增加合作。现在最大的问题或者现在解决最大问题的最大举措是使系统更加代理，并且路线图有点长，但我们仍然按照每周计划的节奏进行。这些是我们正在关注的事情。这周，主要是……有一个很好的词来形容这一点，我希望得到你的帮助，但是润色，我们本周正在修复错误并润色，这就是周一的计划。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That was actually this week was polish, polish week. I love that. How far is this roadmap that you are now having?
turns.zh: 这实际上是波兰周。我喜欢那个。您现在的路线图进展到什么程度了？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: I mean it's clear over the coming month, but it stretches out three months, but in one month it's probably going to look a bit different.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，在接下来的一个月里，情况会很清楚，但会持续三个月，但一个月后，情况可能会有所不同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. And then what are the tools you use just for folks that want to understand the latest tools? So you said FigJam, what else is in that stack of tools?
turns.zh: 好的。那么对于那些想要了解最新工具的人来说，您使用的工具是什么？所以你说FigJam，那堆工具里还有什么？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: I mean we do so many things in our company in Linear because it's just amazing product. So we do talent application tracking in Linear and after going through and this thing, lot of the other custom-made tools for that Linear and then FigJam.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我们在 Linear 公司做了很多事情，因为它是令人惊叹的产品。因此，我们在 Linear 中进行人才申请跟踪，在经历了这件事之后，我们为该 Linear 和 FigJam 提供了许多其他定制工具。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So simple. How soon until one of your engineers is an agent engineer, an AI Engineer, do you have a sense?
turns.zh: 就这么简单。距离你的一位工程师成为代理工程师、人工智能工程师，你有感觉吗？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: I love to dig into what does that question actually mean? I think we've been talking about, Oh, AI that would require something playing chess, that's AI. If a computer can play chess, that's AI and now that's like, Oh no, that's a chess program and which always shifting this forward and forward. I think anything that a human doesn't do is just a smart computer system, right? When is an software engineer and agent, I think it's always going to be just we're building in... Lovable is just an interface that humans interact with to create the software that they want and then how we solve that, we said going to be an agent under some definition. Yeah, sure. I think so, but that's less important to me.
turns.zh: 我喜欢深入研究这个问题的真正含义是什么？我想我们一直在谈论，哦，人工智能需要下棋，这就是人工智能。如果计算机可以下国际象棋，那就是人工智能，现在就像，哦不，这是一个国际象棋程序，它总是不断地向前推进。我认为任何人类不做的事情都只是智能计算机系统，对吗？什么时候是软件工程师和代理，我认为这总是我们正在构建的……Lovable只是一个界面，人类可以与之交互以创建他们想要的软件，然后我们如何解决这个问题，我们说将成为某种定义下的代理。是的，当然。我想是的，但这对我来说不太重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, I like that. Let me ask this, you guys are moving super fast, scaling like crazy. You described a little bit about your process, weekly planning, FigJam board of ideas and now there's a roadmap that you're kind of thinking out in the future. Is there anything else that you found helps you move this fast that gives you a lot of leverage over the small team you have to ship quickly and move fast that you haven't already mentioned?
turns.zh: 好吧，我喜欢这样。让我问一下，你们的行动速度非常快，疯狂地扩张。您描述了一些有关您的流程、每周计划、FigJam 创意板的信息，现在您正在考虑未来的路线图。您发现还有什么其他事情可以帮助您如此快速地行动，使您对必须快速交付和快速行动的小团队有很大的影响力，而您还没有提到吗？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: We work from the office most of the time. I think it's pretty nice. Then you can say like, "Hey, I think we're thinking wrong about this thing," or, "Shouldn't we actually do this other thing?" And especially I think lunch, eating lunch together is a pretty productive hour where you're cross pollinating. I mean people are constantly thinking subconsciously as well about how to solve these different problems and which the most important ones are. And then being in office has this focus or most of the time usually focus, but you also have this high bandwidth where everyone has to be down structured communication.
turns.zh: 我们大部分时间都在办公室工作。我认为这非常好。然后你可以说，“嘿，我认为我们对这件事的想法是错误的，”或者，“我们实际上不应该做另一件事吗？”尤其是我认为午餐，一起吃午餐是一个非常富有成效的时间，你可以在其中进行异花授粉。我的意思是，人们在潜意识中不断思考如何解决这些不同的问题以及哪些是最重要的问题。然后在办公室有这个焦点，或者大多数时候通常是焦点，但你也有这样的高带宽，每个人都必须进行结构化沟通。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. The answer to the CEO of a company that's one of the most advanced AI tools in the world is one of your answers to how to move fast is lunch together. I love that. That's so human and so it makes all the sense in the world, but I love that that's still a part of this.
turns.zh: 我喜欢那个。世界上最先进的人工智能工具之一的公司的首席执行官对如何快速行动的答案之一就是一起吃午餐。我喜欢那个。这是非常人性化的，所以它在世界上是有意义的，但我喜欢它仍然是其中的一部分。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. You talked about this kind of on the same thread you talked about if you were to start a team, like a new product team today, say you were head of product somewhere or head of RPM, VP of product somewhere building a new product team, scaling a product team, what would you do going forward that's different from what people have done in the past in terms of who you're hiring, how you're structuring them, that kind of thing? Just what do you think people should be thinking as they build product teams going forward? Knowing tools like Lovable exist and all the other stuff that's going on.
turns.zh: 好的。你在同一主题上谈到了这一点，如果你要组建一个团队，比如今天的一个新产品团队，假设你是某处的产品负责人或 RPM 负责人、某处的产品副总裁，建立一个新的产品团队，扩展一个产品团队，你会做什么与人们过去所做的不同，比如你要雇用谁，你如何构建他们，诸如此类的事情？您认为人们在未来建立产品团队时应该思考什么？了解像 Lovable 这样的工具的存在以及所有其他正在发生的事情。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: I mean everyone should be excited about using AI. I think that's a pretty big ones. And then the team working really well together is, like the lunch, you have to sit down and solve problems together. The bottleneck for most products these days is not going to be as much on engineering, but having good taste, good intuition about your users. And that, engineers and everyone preferably in the team should have that willingness at least to want to go through that motion and listen to the users and truly understand what they care about.
turns.zh: 我的意思是每个人都应该对使用人工智能感到兴奋。我认为这是一个相当大的。然后团队合作得非常好，就像午餐一样，你必须坐下来一起解决问题。如今，大多数产品的瓶颈不再是工程，而是拥有良好的品味和对用户的良好直觉。而且，工程师和团队中的每个人（最好是团队中的每个人）都应该至少愿意完成该动议并倾听用户的意见并真正理解他们所关心的内容。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well it's kind of like the background of most of the engineers and people you've hired. Is there anything in common? Are they just super impressive humans generally, like champions of programming contests, stuff like that? I don't know. What are some attributes of the folks you've hired so far?
turns.zh: 嗯，这有点像您雇用的大多数工程师和人员的背景。有什么共同点吗？他们是不是一般都是令人印象深刻的人，比如编程竞赛的冠军之类的？我不知道。到目前为止，您雇用的员工有哪些特质？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: I think raw cognitive capability is the strongest, the strongest correlate of being at Lovable. But there is this startup mindset that I think is also very strong. Being much more interested in moving very fast and iterating fast, then having a lot of structure, a lot of process and thinking about the business as a whole. More than thinking about my specific profession, my specific craft that I'm seeing myself wanting to dig into on me.
turns.zh: 我认为原始认知能力是最强大的，是与可爱相关的最强的。但我认为这种创业心态也非常强烈。对快速移动和快速迭代更感兴趣，然后有很多结构、很多流程并从整体上思考业务。不仅仅是考虑我的特定职业、我的特定技能，我发现自己想要深入研究我的技能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Okay. So smart, very smart entrepreneurial, acts like an owner, isn't just like, this isn't just a job. But they feel like they actually have agency. Okay, this is great. There's something you said kind of along these lines that I think is important that one of the things that gets you excited about what you're building is giving people super powers and especially people that don't add a code, basically 99% of people. Is there anything along those lines that you think is important to share?
turns.zh: 惊人的。好的。如此聪明，非常聪明的企业家，表现得像一个所有者，不仅仅是，这不仅仅是一份工作。但他们觉得自己确实有代理权。好的，这太棒了。你所说的类似内容我认为很重要，让你对你正在构建的东西感到兴奋的事情之一就是赋予人们超能力，特别是那些不添加代码的人，基本上是 99% 的人。您认为有什么值得分享的重要内容吗？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: It's very clear to most people who have been engineers or been founders, that there's so many that have failed in their endeavors because they didn't have someone that know how to solve the technical parts. And now that we're close to having people know that this exists and they solve everything, it's going to be an Cambrian explosion of entrepreneurship and better software product. We're not going to settle for all the annoying bad technology that we use today. And everyone who has an idea is going to say, "Okay, I'm going to build this thing and show you that this is the best version of the product or what our company should be doing," instead of having long meetings or writing up documents. So it's going to be empowering across a lot of different professions and places in the world.
turns.zh: 对于大多数曾经担任过工程师或创始人的人来说，很清楚，有很多人在他们的努力中失败了，因为他们没有人知道如何解决技术部分。现在我们已经接近让人们知道这个存在并且他们解决了所有问题，这将是创业精神和更好的软件产品的寒武纪爆发。我们不会满足于今天使用的所有烦人的糟糕技术。每个有想法的人都会说，“好吧，我要构建这个东西并向您展示这是该产品的最佳版本或我们公司应该做的事情”，而不是召开长时间的会议或编写文档。因此，它将为世界上许多不同职业和地方提供支持。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's next for Lovable? What's the next few things they might launch as this episode comes out?
turns.zh: 可爱的下一步是什么？随着这一集的播出，他们接下来可能会推出什么？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: As I mentioned this agentic behavior, and when I say agentic, what it means is that you give more freedom to the system to decide what happens next. It might want to write a test, run those tests and say like, "Oh, the test failed, let's fix those." So that's one of the big unlocks for getting further faster. And then there's some more obvious things that you want to do to go all the way to easily go all the way to making money with Lovable. And that's like how do you set up so that it's hosted on your specific domain? How do you collaborate there seamlessly with your team and making that is here so that those are just obvious things and something we're thinking about is to help founders succeed after they built their first version. And how do they get more users? How do they get feedback? How do they get the word out if they build something useful?
turns.zh: 正如我提到的这种代理行为，当我说代理时，它的意思是你给系统更多的自由来决定接下来会发生什么。它可能想要编写一个测试，运行这些测试并说，“哦，测试失败了，让我们修复它们。”因此，这是获得更快速度的重要解锁之一。然后还有一些更明显的事情是你想做的，以便一路轻松地一路通过 Lovable 赚钱。这就像如何设置才能将其托管在您的特定域上？您如何与您的团队无缝协作，并在此处实现这一点，以便这些都是显而易见的事情，我们正在考虑的事情是帮助创始人在构建第一个版本后取得成功。他们如何获得更多用户？他们如何获得反馈？如果他们构建了一些有用的东西，他们如何宣传？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I was just going to say that and that's exactly where my mind went is everyone's going to be building all these things. No one's ever going to get any traction with these tools. No one knows how to find users, get anyone to basically go to market. And growth is a whole different skill. So that is so cool that you're thinking about that. How do we run some paid ads for you? How do we think about SEO? How do we think about word of mouth, reality referrals? That is very cool. Okay.
turns.zh: 我正要这么说，而这正是我的想法：每个人都会建造所有这些东西。没有人会对这些工具产生任何吸引力。没有人知道如何找到用户，如何让任何人基本上进入市场。成长是一种完全不同的技能。所以你正在考虑这个真是太酷了。我们如何为您投放一些付费广告？我们如何看待SEO？我们如何看待口碑、现实推荐？这非常酷。好的。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: Yeah, we already have playbooks that we help the people building with how do you do those things that you can find up on our blog?
turns.zh: 是的，我们已经有了可以帮助人们构建的剧本，您可以在我们的博客上找到如何做这些事情？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interestingly, this makes me want to buy some meta stock because all these apps that everyone's building, they're going to be running paid ads on Facebook and Google. Oh my god, what a good business those other guys get. I want to come back to, you said that you can work on your existing code base. This is actually a big question for a lot of people. They see all these tools, they're all amazing for prototypes and concepting. You talked about how you can actually do this within your existing code base, use Lovable.
turns.zh: 有趣的是，这让我想购​​买一些元股票，因为每个人都在构建的所有这些应用程序都将在 Facebook 和 Google 上运行付费广告。天啊，其他人的生意真是太好了。我想回到你说的，你可以在现有的代码库上工作。这其实是很多人的一个大问题。他们看到了所有这些工具，它们对于原型和概念来说都令人惊叹。您谈到了如何在现有代码库中使用 Lovable 来实际执行此操作。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: Let me correct you there. You cannot use it on any existing code base.
turns.zh: 让我纠正你一下。您不能在任何现有代码库上使用它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it.
turns.zh: 知道了。

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: We kind of have a research preview of importing your code base, but what you can do is if you start in Lovable, then you can have engineers editing it in whatever tool they want to use for editing it.
turns.zh: 我们有一个导入代码库的研究预览，但你可以做的是，如果你从 Lovable 开始，那么你可以让工程师在他们想要用来编辑它的任何工具中编辑它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, cool. That's great clarification. So I guess just for people, because most listeners here are not building something brand new, they're working within an existing product. So you're saying that that is coming, you can use Lovable in the future in some form with your existing app and product?
turns.zh: 好吧，酷。这是很好的澄清。所以我想只是针对人们，因为这里的大多数听众并不是在构建全新的东西，他们是在现有的产品中工作。所以你是说，这即将到来，你将来可以在现有的应用程序和产品中以某种形式使用 Lovable 吗？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: Correct.
turns.zh: 正确的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, that's huge. Okay. Because basically most people, so that's going to be a big deal. Okay. Final question. We have the segment on this podcast called Failure Corner, where most people come to this podcast, they show all these stories of success and everything's going great, and here's all the things always winning. You guys, this is a good example, just up into the right, the fastest growing product ever. What's an example when something totally failed in the course of your career and what did you learn from that?
turns.zh: 哇，那太大了。好的。因为基本上是大多数人，所以这将是一件大事。好的。最后一个问题。我们在这个播客上有一个名为“失败角落”的部分，大多数人都会来看这个播客，他们展示了所有这些成功的故事，一切都进展顺利，而这里是所有总是获胜的事情。你们，这是一个很好的例子，刚刚进入正确的、有史以来增长最快的产品。在您的职业生涯中，有什么事情完全失败的例子吗？您从中学到了什么？

turns.speaker: Anton Osika
turns.en: I am a bit hard-pressed to find something that totally failed, but I think there's a bit of a product lesson where I was the first employee at an AI startup here in Stockholm called Summer Labs, and the premise was just, okay, so humans learn in different ways. If you personalize, then you get two standard deviations more effective learning. So there are a lot of products like education software that helps you learn that is not personalized. And we were building an API to personalize learning and the AI and so on, it was pretty good. (01:02:34): But the thing that we were doing in the end was to say like, Okay, here's this product. Someone has to build a product or some way to learn or be it like English thing Duolingo, and then the people that have that product have to use this advanced AI API to start making it personalized. And it is very hard retrofitting like, oh, you have to switch out the engine and put in this AI. And the big learning here is that it didn't work very well for the company. I mean, the company wasn't super successful in this. The big learning is that you have to start with how is this product working end-to-end and then add AI or think where should we add AI? So that was a big learning for me that you really want to see what does the big picture of the user, what's the big picture of how do you think the user experience should be? And then add something with AI to solve specific problems. And now Summer Labs is doing great, but it's not on top of that product specifically.
turns.zh: 我很难找到完全失败的东西，但我认为有一些产品课程，我是斯德哥尔摩一家名为 Summer Labs 的人工智能初创公司的第一位员工，前提是，好吧，所以人类以不同的方式学习。如果你个性化，那么你会得到两个标准差的更有效的学习。所以有很多像教育软件这样的产品可以帮助你学习，但这些产品并不是个性化的。我们正在构建一个 API 来个性化学习和人工智能等，这非常好。 (01:02:34)：但我们最终要做的就是说，好吧，这是这个产品。有人必须构建一个产品或某种学习方式，或者像英语的 Duolingo 一样，然后拥有该产品的人必须使用这个先进的 AI API 来开始使其个性化。这是非常困难的改造，就像，哦，你必须关闭引擎并放入这个人工智能。这里最大的教训是它对公司来说效果不佳。我的意思是，该公司在这方面并不是非常成功。最重要的学习是，你必须从这个产品端到端如何工作开始，然后添加人工智能，或者思考我们应该在哪里添加人工智能？所以这对我来说是一个很大的学习，你真的想了解用户的总体情况是什么，你认为用户体验应该如何？然后用人工智能添加一些东西来解决特定的问题。现在夏季实验室做得很好，但它还没有专门超越该产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think it's a lot of people hear this and they're like, of course, but I think it's so hard to actually remember this point when you have some cool tech and you're like, "Holy shit, everyone needs to try this. They're going to love it." And then you don't realize no one actually cares if it's not solving a problem for them. There's a lot of novelty products that everyone want to use for a little bit and then forget instant, I don't actually need this often. And so what this makes me think about is, there's all these product lessons for what is likely to help your product be successful. And an app like a tool like Lovable can help you do this because if someone is building something, you can guide them, Okay, what's the problem you're solving for somebody? How many people have this problem? How much does this matter to them?
turns.zh: 我想很多人听到这个之后都会想，当然，但是我认为当你拥有一些很酷的技术并且你会想，“天哪，每个人都需要尝试这个。他们会喜欢它的”时，要真正记住这一点是非常困难的。然后你不会意识到没有人真正关心这是否没有为他们解决问题。有很多新奇的产品，每个人都想用一下，然后就忘记了，我实际上并不经常需要这个。因此，这让我想到的是，所有这些产品课程都可能有助于您的产品取得成功。像 Lovable 这样的工具之类的应用程序可以帮助你做到这一点，因为如果有人正在构建某些东西，你可以指导他们，好吧，你正在为某人解决什么问题？有多少人有这个问题？这对他们来说有多重要？
